source.name: beyond-all-reason/spring (Recoil engine)
source.status: historical candidate; not installed or current

components.title: Per-client synchronized factory submission
components.summary: Each client handling the authenticated replacement packet resolves the origin authority and applies the decoded Replace or Fence submission to its local synchronized service.

components.title: Local callback ownership boundary
components.summary: The public factory read callbacks require the currently executing local AI identity and resolve it through the local player, preventing peer B from using this surface to read peer A's origin AI slot.

components.title: CREG service-state carrier
components.summary: Serializes authority, fence, high-water and result-ring state into the game-state collector and verifies a single synthetic authority round trip.

flows.title: Authenticated peer apply, local read boundary and conditional save carrier

steps.description: Receive the synchronized packet on a client, validate origin player/AI identity, decode it and apply it to the local service.
Require the requested AI to equal the currently executing AI and resolve that AI through the local player before any callback read.
Read a keyed Replace or Fence result only after the local callback ownership context succeeds.
Serialize authority incarnation, high-water, fence state and every occupied canonical result wire.
Include the factory replacement service in the real CREG game-state collector after AI handler state.
Exercise one synthetic authority's fence result and exact replay classification across an in-memory save/load round trip.

facts.statement: The synchronized network handler resolves the packet's origin player and AI, checks incarnation, and applies the submission without requiring the origin player to equal the receiving client's local player.
Factory snapshot/result callbacks require the currently executing AI ID and resolve it with gu->myPlayerNum; native AIs are loaded only for the local player's registered AI set.

A receiving peer can apply the origin AI's synchronized submission to its local service copy, but peer B cannot use the public AI callback to read peer A's origin AI state because callback ownership is local. An independent peer result/fence observation therefore needs another source-grounded seam.
CREG serialization includes per-authority incarnation, high-water, fence watermark, active fence epoch/expiry and each stored Replace or Fence result's canonical wire bytes.

CREG is only a conditional carrier for paired proof: the indexed test shows one synthetic authority round trip, while these sources do not establish matched saves from two actual peers, completed custody, or a bounded offline extractor.

open_questions: Will a bounded diagnostic at the authenticated per-peer dispatch record before/after service state and keyed results without changing synchronized behavior?
If CREG is used instead, where is the deterministic typed offline extractor and how are matched peer boundaries and file custody proven?
